activities.anchor: Between those two sits every dosing decision, every interaction warning
activities.caption: drag across the drug's two paired sciences
activities.name: pharmAdmeCompare

config.prompt: Drag across the journey and its effect:

before.label: what the body does to the drug
before.text: Pharmacokinetics, in four letters: ADME — absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion.

after.label: what the drug does to the body
after.text: Pharmacodynamics: which receptors it touches and how strongly — the effect on arrival.

config.why: A drug is not a substance so much as a journey — and every 'take with food' instruction a pharmacist gives lives between the two sciences.

activities.anchor: Same target organ, same disease, dramatically better drug
activities.caption: sequence the engineering of salbutamol
activities.name: pharmSarOrder

config.prompt: From adrenaline to a selective inhaler, in order:
items: Adrenaline relieves bronchospasm powerfully — but stimulates all adrenergic receptors: racing heart, tremor
Medicinal chemistry untangles the receptor family: β1 mostly cardiac, β2 mostly bronchial
A ring change (saligenin for catechol) plus a bulkier N-substituent
Salbutamol — β2-selective enough to open airways at doses that largely spare the heart
config.why: Structure–activity relationships make drug design reasoning rather than luck — one modification at a time, measured each time.

activities.anchor: The numbers are heuristics, routinely broken by successful exceptions
activities.caption: guess the magnitude — Lipinski's weight flag
activities.name: pharmLipinskiEstimate

config.prompt: Lipinski's 'rule of five' flags oral absorption trouble when molecular weight exceeds roughly…
config.why: About 500 in molecular weight, 5 hydrogen-bond donors, 10 acceptors, logP of 5 — a membrane must be crossed, and membranes are choosy.
config.context: the central tension: water-soluble enough to travel in blood, fat-soluble enough to cross lipid membranes

activities.anchor: the pipe narrows, so the flow must
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the four legs
activities.name: pharmLegsCloze

config.text: An intravenous dose is %%0%% percent bioavailable by definition; an oral dose must survive stomach acid, the gut wall and the liver's %%1%% metabolism. Only %%2%% drug is active and clearable, and renal impairment is the classic reason for dose %%3%%.
config.hint: The IV fraction, the great filter, the binding rule, and what the kidney's narrowing forces.

activities.anchor: so the effect persists after the drug is long gone
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the 20-minute drug
activities.name: pharmAspirinPredict

config.q: Aspirin's plasma half-life is about 20 minutes. How long does a single dose's anti-platelet effect last?
choices: The platelet's entire 7-to-10-day lifespan — the molecule binds irreversibly
config.why: Duration of action is a pharmacodynamic property — set by receptor residency and physiology, not by concentration alone.

activities.anchor: The pharmacist's interaction check is applied enzymology
activities.caption: file each interaction by its CYP move
activities.name: pharmCypSort

config.prompt: Shared enzymes, two directions — file each:

items.label: inhibit CYP3A4 and a co-administered statin accumulates toward muscle damage
grapefruit juice blocks CYP3A4 in the gut wall for a day or more
the enzyme churns faster and clears the other drug before it works
the documented way St John's wort undermines oral contraceptives

config.why: Enzymes are shared resources — the main arena of drug–drug interactions, and the moment ADME theory becomes a life-saving reflex.

activities.anchor: drugs with narrow indices (warfarin, digoxin, lithium, insulin) demand monitoring of levels
activities.caption: pair each pharmacodynamic term with its definition
activities.name: pharmCurveMatch

config.prompt: Reading the dose–response curve — pair them:

pairs.right: the concentration giving half-maximal effect — how much drug it takes
the ceiling — how much effect is possible even in principle
activates the receptor (morphine at the μ-opioid receptor)
occupies without activating — naloxone evicting opioids to reverse an overdose
tops down an overactive system while substituting for a missing one (buprenorphine)

config.why: A potent drug needs a small dose; only a high-efficacy drug can produce a large effect — and no dose of a partial agonist ever matches a full one.

activities.anchor: Sterile preparations add asepsis as an absolute requirement
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the formulation note
activities.name: pharmFormSpot

config.prompt: One line of this formulation note is wrong — click it:
lines: Dissolution rate gates how fast a solid can begin to work.
Coatings decide where in the gut the dose releases.
Excipients are inert filler, so formulation choices never change onset or safety.
Modified-release design stretches one dose over 24 hours by engineering the exit ramp.
Bioavailability is where chemistry, manufacturing and patient technique meet.
config.correction: Excipients control flow, stability and disintegration — the form is part of the drug, and substitution between extended-release brands is a pharmacy decision, not a formality.
config.why: Formulation is the engineering of absorption: dissolution, release site, excipients and modified-release design change onset, duration and even safety.
